additional_concerns: Footnote 3 is supplied in da12aecad4e68.u30.3569. The XML and web-form claims' missing-footnote uncertainties are stale. Its markers attach to XML and PDF, not the web form.

The XML permission is supported as a permitted-method statement, but its extracted conditions omit the required e-Cert. If those conditions are intended as exhaustive sufficient conditions, that stronger reading is contradicted by footnote 3. This extraction issue does not make XML permission relevant to a resubmission-trigger question.

Both compliance candidates expressly exclude XML-schema conformity from their XML facts. Their results address the selected channel, method and e-Cert control, not all XML obligations. The separate schema and technical-test requirements must not be inferred satisfied.

The separate JFIU XML schema, prescribed PDF form and operational e-Cert instructions are unavailable. The opaque dependency IDs cannot reliably be mapped to these materials. What materials and dependency mappings establish those classifications?

Footnote 3 requires an e-Cert but does not specify the operational manner of use. The submission-specific supplied-or-used condition in node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5 requires further authority; it should not silently become an additional substantive restriction.

The date-only trigger includes filings before 9:00am on 2 February 2026. The source distinguishes a date-effective channel rule, a 9:00am operational launch and resubmission following implementation. Preserve competing interpretations; the date-only candidate cannot distinguish the morning blackout from operational launch.

The timestamp candidates select the operational-launch interpretation. The governing timezone and exact inclusive boundary are not expressly resolved in the packet. What JFIU clarification establishes those details and the relationship between the date-effective provision and operational launch?
Urgent blackout contact is permitted but does not itself establish an actual STR submission. Automatic migration likewise does not establish a new submission event.
The history candidate establishes whether a trigger ever existed, not whether a duty remains outstanding after resubmission. FALSE requires sufficient history to exclude qualifying events.
Non-filing events return FALSE in node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb but OUT_OF_SCOPE in the other event candidates. This domain difference should remain explicit.
Rule-wide conflict blocking may prevent evaluation despite an otherwise sufficient alternative method. That runtime policy is not a substantive restriction established by the circular.
